title: Analyst + press briefings plan (outreach list, deck, embargo, speaker prep, quote approvals)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
- Coordinate analyst + press briefings for the Latency/$ benchmark report launch with consistent, defensible claims.
- Produce an outreach list, briefing deck, embargo plan, speaker prep/Q&A, and get quotes/claims approved.

Why
- Analysts/press will pressure-test methodology and claims; we need a crisp narrative + credible methodology posture.
- Reduce last-minute churn by locking: (1) what we will and won’t claim, (2) who says what, (3) what is shared under embargo.

Deliverables (this ticket)
1) Analyst outreach list + prioritization
- Tier 1: AI infra / LLM platforms, cloud infra, developer tooling.
- Tier 2: procurement/FinOps adjacent analysts who will care about unit economics framing.
- For each: firm, analyst name, focus area, relationship owner, last touch date, preferred format, time zone.

2) Briefing materials
- Analyst briefing deck (20–25 mins + 20 mins Q&A)
  - Market framing: why production economics > model access
  - Methodology credibility (high level + appendix)
  - Headline findings (ensure variance language + constraints)
  - What’s next (refresh cadence, coverage roadmap)
- Press briefing one-pager (short narrative, approved stats, disclosures) + press release alignment.

3) Embargo plan
- Embargo date/time aligned with launch go-live.
- What can be shared pre-embargo (deck, PDF, selected charts) and what cannot (full tables, internal QA artifacts).
- Tracking: who received which materials + acknowledgement.

4) Speaker prep
- Identify speakers and roles:
  - Camila Reyes: opening narrative + GTM framing
  - Jonas Weber: methodology guardrails + limitations
  - Claire Dubois: benchmark execution/QA + variance
  - (Optional) Jordan Blake: customer outcomes + what Sales will do next
- Prep doc with:
  - talk track by slide
  - “tough questions” section (variance, cherry-picking, cost assumptions, region deltas, competitor comparisons)
  - redlines on what we do NOT say

5) Quotes + claims approval workflow
- Collect quote drafts (CRO/VP Marketing/VP Applied ML placeholders) and route for approval.
- Ensure alignment with: Public benchmarking claims guidelines + core messaging.
- Final sign-off: Marketing (Camila) + Methodology sponsor (Jonas) + Legal (Michael Grant).

Key inputs / references
- Analyst deck draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/analyst-briefing-deck-v1.json
- Press release draft: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/go-to-market/press-release-draft.json
- Messaging guardrails: sources/confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/benchmark-report-core-messaging.json
- External claims guidelines: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/performance-standards/public-benchmarking-claims-guidelines.json
- Competitive FAQ (for Q&A prep): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/competitive/benchmark-report-competitive-faq.json
- Methodology canonical doc: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/latency-per-dollar-benchmark-methodology.json

Non-goals
- We are not publishing raw logs, per-request traces, or anything that could be reverse-engineered to identify customers.
- We are not making absolute "best overall" claims without confidence intervals and scope constraints.

Acceptance criteria (Definition of Done)
- Outreach list finalized (Tiering + owners) and first wave scheduled.
- Briefing deck vFinal approved (Marketing + Applied ML + Legal).
- Embargo language locked + included in outreach email.
- Speaker prep completed with a dry run and updated Q&A doc.
- Quotes approved in writing (email) and incorporated consistently across press/blog/deck.

Risks / watchouts
- Analysts will ask for raw tables and/or methodology details beyond what we want public. Prep an explicit escalation path and what we can share under NDA vs not.
- Avoid implying results generalize to all workloads. We should repeat: “representative workloads,” “within stated config,” “variance observed,” “repro steps available.”
- Region comparisons can be misread as “Redwood slower in X.” Ensure we explain underlying trade-offs (capacity windows, hardware, routing policies) and how customers should interpret regional data.

Owner notes
- Camila owns the overall press/analyst motion; Ben supports scheduling + UTMs; Ethan supports narrative coherence; Jonas/Claire own methodology truthfulness; Michael owns legal review + claims language.
